parsed.explanation: The operative regime is federal hostility with state-level service protections. Federal document/entry rules, passport marker binary, visa discrepancy/fraud exposure, government-funded single-sex facility restrictions and severe reported custody practices are traveler-facing universal or high-severity exposures. Local anti-discrimination/public-accommodation law, penalty enhancement, no facility ban and marker-change practice reduce local friction but do not cancel federal screening, federal facilities or federal/immigration detention. For a minor or parent, local care and conversion-therapy protections matter, yet national border and federal-program rules remain. Overall high risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal sex-marker policy bars X for new passports/visas and processes by assigned sex; discrepancy/reasonable doubt can trigger refusal, additional evidence, and permanent-fraud findings. Existing X may be valid but scrutinized.
entry_documents.protection: AC LU suit and legal-aid FAQ show contest; no documented travel exemption; foreign advisories indicate exposure not resolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening can move into fraud investigation, detention, or removal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections/immigration reports birth-sex/conversion-style placement, forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse. Any detention after border mismatch risks federal custody severity.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State law no facility ban and bias-crime penalties, but no state placement/monitoring documented; protections do not cover federal custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document/care encounter may trigger investigation; final detention placement under federal rules dominates.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order restricts government-funded single-sex facilities by assigned sex; airport/federal/state-aided facilities may apply despite state no-ban map.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State equality map records no state/provincial bathroom ban; public-accommodation law and commission protect ordinary venues.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local/state private facilities safer, but federal facilities and security screening remain universal-exposure.

care_services.exposure: National hostility to youth care, funding/insurance threats, records subpoenas; adult emergency/ward placement not documented. Federal programs apply.
care_services.protection: State conversion-therapy ban and insurance non-discrimination indicate local care climate; no documented traveler remedy for federal barriers.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking minor/guardian can lead to document checks or reporting; local providers may be safer, federal not.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders and counterterrorism language frame gender identity policy as forbidden/extremist; document/fraud rules can be used against travelers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State anti-discrimination and bias-crime enhancement; no local hostile enforcement documented; some national orders blocked.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing may influence border/custody and local referrals; state protections reduce but do not erase.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor or guardian can face border document scrutiny and national youth-care criminalization/funding threats; school/health encounters may out family.
minors_guardians.protection: State converts conversion therapy to unprofessional conduct, protects insurance, no facility ban; family-facing local protections may help.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent/guardian can become investigated subject through child documents/care; state protections don't preempt federal entry or custody.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No local incident/enforcement figures; national hostility and support for birth-sex documents may raise confrontations; police response undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State public-accommodation ban and bias-crime penalty create recourse; no state targeting documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street violence is state-handled, but document/security exposure is federal; absence of reports is not safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Permanent-fraud waivers limited; many court challenges unresolved; state enforcement and custody/facility outcomes unknown; X-marker and panic-defence statuses stale.
remedies_unknowns.protection: AC LU suit, legal-aid FAQ, state commission/laws; complaint routes exist but not proven to change outcomes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved remedies mean routine document or facility questions can escalate before relief.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.35-A’s birth-sex facility rule, but federal border/fraud screening and custody abuse raise severity; local anti-discrimination/no state ban lower local facility exposure. Slightly below 0.35.

More dangerous than 0.45-A: 0.45-A has a public-building bathroom rule with no criminal border/fraud/custody exposure. Here federal entry screening, fraud findings, government-funded facility rules and severe custody reports dominate.

Higher than 0.25-D because local facilities/public accommodations are protective and no local presentation offence is documented, though federal border/custody exposure prevents reduced-risk placement.

parsed.synthesis: Layering means federal rules operate at the border, in security/federal programs and federal custody, while state law mostly governs private/state services. The traveller’s worst-case exposure—document mismatch, possible fraud finding, federal birth-sex facilities and abusive custody—remains reachable even in a protective state. Local remedies help in hotels, shops and state buildings, but no documented state mechanism offsets federal screening or detention. The score sits in High Risk, above jurisdictions with local universal bans, because protective state machinery is real but incomplete.
